read.sections.2.text.back: A wide view helps us see patterns, that is, changes that repeat or last for a long time. Maps from different years can show Riverstone slowly spreading to the other side of the river. But a wide view can also hide people, because a timeline cannot show every person's choices. Some historians look from very far away, up to the whole history of the universe. At that scale, one town is too small to be seen. That is why historians move from one scale to another. No scale is always better, because the best scale depends on the question you ask.
read.sections.2.text.source: A wide view helps us see a pattern, which is a change that repeats or goes on for a long time. Maps from many different years can show Riverstone slowly spreading across the river. But a wide view can also hide people, because a line on a timeline cannot show every person's choices. Some historians zoom out as far as possible, to the whole history of the universe. At that scale, one town is far too small to see. That is why historians move between scales. Neither scale is always better, because the best scale depends on the question you ask.

watch.summary.note: "Scientists explain" uses "Para ilmuwan menjelaskan", as in Lesson 4. "The universe began" is "alam semesta bermula".
watch.summary.back: This short video uses the widest scale: the history of the whole universe. Scientists explain that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago. At first, the universe was very small and very hot. Then the universe became bigger and cooler. Since then, the universe has kept changing. At this scale, you do not see a single person, town or country. You only see very big changes over billions of years. This helps us see that human history is a small part of a much longer story. But this scale cannot tell us why a trader was late, or how a family lived. To find out those things, historians look close up.
watch.summary.source: This short video uses the widest scale there is: the history of the whole universe. Scientists explain that the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago. At first, it was very small and very hot. Then it grew bigger and cooler. It has kept changing ever since. At this scale, you do not see any person, town or country. You see only very big changes over billions of years. This helps us see that human history is a small part of a much longer story. But this scale cannot tell us why one trader was late, or how one family lived. To learn those things, historians zoom in.

read.sections.0.text.back: On a map on a screen, you can zoom: enlarge the view to see one street, or shrink it to see a whole country. Historians do something similar with the past, because they choose a scale. Scale means how big a part of time, place or group you decide to study. A close scale looks at one day, one letter or one family. A wide scale can follow one town for 100 years, or compare many regions over thousands of years. Look at Riverstone. At the scale of one afternoon, the story is about rain and a closed bridge. Over 20 years, the story is about a growing town. Over several hundred years, the story is about a river that moves.
read.sections.0.text.source: On a map on a screen, you can zoom in to see one street or zoom out to see a whole country. Historians do something similar with the past, because they choose a scale. Scale means how big a piece of time, place or group you decide to study. A close scale looks at one day, one letter or one family. A wide scale might follow a whole town for 100 years, or compare many regions over thousands of years. Look at Riverstone. At the scale of one afternoon, the story is about rain and a closed bridge. Over 20 years, it is about a town that grows. Over several hundred years, it is about a river that moves.

read.sections.0.simpler.back: On a map, you can zoom. You can make the map bigger or smaller. Historians also do this with the past. They choose a scale. Scale means how much time or place you look at. A close scale is one day or one family. A wide scale is one town for 100 years. In Riverstone, the story of one afternoon is about rain and a bridge. Over 20 years, the town grew. Over hundreds of years, the river moved.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: On a map, you can zoom in and out. Historians do this with the past too. They choose a scale. Scale means how much time or place you look at. A close scale is one day or one family. A wide scale is a town over 100 years. In Riverstone, the story of one afternoon is about rain and a bridge. Over 20 years, the town grows. Over hundreds of years, the river moves.

read.sections.1.text.back: A close view helps us notice choices, feelings and small details in people's lives. A diary, a receipt or one photo can show how an event changed someone's day. For example, a trader's diary might say that she waited six hours until the bridge opened. But the day one person experienced is not always the same as other people's day. Another trader might choose to take the long road. So close-up evidence needs context, meaning we need to know what was happening around it at that time.
read.sections.1.text.source: A close view helps us notice people's choices, feelings and small details. A diary, a receipt or one photograph can show how an event changed one person's day. For example, a trader's diary might say that she waited six hours for the bridge to open. However, one person's day is not always the same as everyone else's. Other traders may have taken the long road instead. So close evidence needs context, which means we need to know what was happening around it at the time.

read.sections.1.simpler.back: A close view shows people. We see their choices and feelings. A diary or receipt shows one person's day. A trader might wait six hours at the bridge. But another trader might take the long road. One person's day is not the same as everyone's day. So we need context. Context is what happened around that source.

read.sections.2.simpler.back: A wide view shows patterns. A pattern is a change that lasts a long time. Maps from many years show the town getting bigger. But a wide view can hide people. A timeline cannot show every person. Some historians look at the whole universe. There, one town cannot be seen at all. So historians move from close to wide. The best scale depends on your question.

write.example.back: At the one-afternoon scale, we see heavy rain and a closed bridge. A trader had to go by a longer road, so she arrived late. Over 20 years, the evidence shows a town that is growing. New houses and markets spread to both sides of the river. A close scale helps us answer why a trader was late that day. A wide scale helps us answer why Riverstone built two new bridges. Put together, the two scales show that one place can have more than one story.
write.example.source: At the scale of one afternoon, we notice heavy rain and a closed bridge. A trader has to take a longer road, so she arrives late. Over 20 years, the evidence shows a town that is growing. New homes and markets spread to both sides of the river. The close scale helps us answer why one trader was late that day. The wide scale helps us answer why Riverstone built two new bridges. Together, the two scales show that one place can have more than one story.
